clue.text: Design feature lacking a free counter

definitions.note: verb sense: to counter an argument is to rebut it

indicators.note: to design is to plan or lay out afresh, so the letters left over are rearranged

explanation.surface: An architectural feature is missing its free-standing counter or worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a' takes the A out of FEATURE, leaving FETURE, which 'Design' rearranges; 'free' supports the rearrangement. 'counter' looks like a noun (a worktop) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut an argument is to counter it, the verb sense of disproving.

clue.text: Get rid of rage outside — hurry up!

indicators.note: the outside of the word rage means only its first and last letters are used

parts.note: 'Move!' is an order to hurry up

explanation.surface: Someone angrily tells another to get rid of something, and fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rage outside' looks like a container instruction but supplies just the first and last letters of 'rage', R and E, which go before MOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something away is to eliminate it, synonyms for disposing of an item.

clue.text: Striker to fix support for formula one circuit

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath the rest, so this piece comes last

parts.note: Formula One is written F1, read here as the letters FI
a ring is a circuit or circle
to pin is to fix in place

explanation.surface: A racing team's striker is tasked with fixing up support for the Formula One track.
explanation.walkthrough: Formula One is written F1, and the digit stands in for the letter I. In a down answer, something that gives 'support for' the rest sits underneath it, so the fixing piece comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: In a gun the firing pin is the part that strikes the cartridge primer.

clue.text: Short story and opera song. Shoes by Hermes

indicators.note: a short version of the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A list of artistic forms ends with footwear by a fashion house.
explanation.walkthrough: Hermes is not the fashion house but the messenger god of Greek myth, who wore winged sandals.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these were the winged sandals worn by the messenger god.

clue.text: Blackened and marked around the central heating

indicators.note: around tells us the first piece wraps about the second

parts.note: to score is to mark with lines or notches
CH is the standard abbreviation for central heating, as in estate agents' listings

explanation.surface: A boiler fault has left the surroundings of the heating system charred.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charred by fire or heat has been burnt black on its surface.

clue.text: Police officer quietly delayed writing

parts.note: copper is British slang for a police officer
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
late means delayed or behind time

explanation.surface: A constable quietly put off writing up his report.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of elegant, flowing handwriting named after engraved metal printing plates.

clue.text: Like a monarch, one has a number of accoutrements

parts.note: regal means kingly or fit for a monarch
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A king or queen, being royal, owns plenty of finery.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial trappings and insignia of royalty, such as crown and sceptre.

clue.text: Male with skill and courage

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A man possessing ability and bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and spirit, as in 'take heart' or 'lose heart'.

clue.text: Force out one's labour leader in deceitful scheme

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces before it go inside the scheme

parts.note: a dodge is a trick or scam
one is I, so one's is IS

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A politician ousts a Labour Party leader through an underhand plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to remove or push from a fixed position.

clue.text: Cut off additional beer to engender team spirit

indicators.note: the word is cut off short, losing its last letter

parts.note: more means additional or extra
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Stopping extra drinks to build team bonding.
explanation.definitionFit: The confidence and enthusiasm of a group of people.

clue.text: How one might view transparent material given to agent

indicators.note: the material is handed over to the agent, so it is attached after that piece

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
glass is a transparent material

explanation.surface: Giving a see-through substance to a secret agent affects how they see things.
explanation.definitionFit: A small telescope, an instrument for looking at distant things.

clue.text: Shattered relic by opening chamber

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken artefact is found next to the entrance to a tomb chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattered' looks like it describes the relic, but it is the anagram signal; 'by' just places the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two lower cavities of the heart, an anatomical chamber.

clue.text: Join snub about independent state

indicators.note: the independent letter comes up against the snub, placed just before it

parts.note: to connect is to join
to cut someone is to snub them

explanation.surface: An instruction to join a snub to someone acting independently.
explanation.walkthrough: Connecticut is a New England state of the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty states of the USA, in New England.

clue.text: Free time put into building toy for children

indicators.note: put into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Lego is a children's construction toy of plastic bricks

explanation.surface: Free time spent playing with a construction toy.
explanation.definitionFit: To release your hold on something is to set it free.

clue.text: Direct aircraft are noisy prior to reaching maximum altitude

indicators.note: being noisy here means the word is heard rather than read, so its sound is used

parts.note: planes are aircraft
peaking means reaching the highest point

explanation.surface: Aircraft roar loudly as they climb to their highest altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are noisy' signals that PLANES is heard, giving PLAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank, straightforward talk, which is direct in manner.

clue.text: Resign — or a muscle bound idiot will appear!

indicators.note: bound means enclosed, so the answer is enclosed within these words

explanation.surface: Give up, or a muscle-bound fool will turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorant or stupid person, a dunce.

clue.text: A cause of pain, as a critic runs out in panic!

indicators.note: panic throws things into disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A theatre critic dashes out in a frenzy, a pain in the neck to all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs out' takes the R from AS A CRITIC; 'in panic' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain along the sciatic nerve down the back of the leg.

clue.text: A doctrine is no substitute for careful reflection

indicators.note: a substitute swaps things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dogma cannot replace thoughtful contemplation.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful thought or deliberation over something.

clue.text: Temporary home one found during school period

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: found during means placed within the other piece

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A temporary residence for someone during term time.
explanation.definitionFit: Provisional, lasting only for an intervening period.

clue.text: Floundering — nor is he near the coast!

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone flounders in the shallows, staying close to shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Close to the shore, as opposed to offshore.

clue.text: Constant prices asked for old cars

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
rates are prices or charges

explanation.surface: Fixed prices demanded for vintage motors.
explanation.definitionFit: Crates is slang for decrepit old vehicles, bangers or jalopies.

clue.text: A look with feet in the air?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A glance with one's feet up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Up high, overhead, the idea of being airborne.

clue.text: Working on radio is a beginning

parts.note: on means working or operating
a radio is a set

explanation.surface: Being on air as a broadcaster is a start.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its start or outbreak.

clue.text: The bursar is more certain to follow exchange rate

indicators.note: this phrase puts the second piece after the first
exchange means swap around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: surer means more certain

explanation.surface: A college finance officer is sure to keep track of the exchange rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange rate' reads as one financial phrase, but 'exchange' is the anagram signal working on 'rate', and 'to follow' puts the comparative after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bursar manages the finances of an institution, a financial officer.

clue.text: This month start thinking about Irish police command

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the police force

parts.note: inst (instant) is the old business abbreviation for this month

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's former police force

explanation.surface: This month someone begins thinking of an order for the Irish police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This month' is old business-letter shorthand (instant). The Royal Ulster Constabulary was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001; 'about' wraps the month and the start of thinking around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct is to order or direct someone.

clue.text: Clever remark found on tomb in ruins

indicators.note: ruins are wrecked structures, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A witty epitaph is discovered on a crumbling grave.
explanation.definitionFit: French for a 'good word', a witty saying.

clue.text: Makes an effort and regularly baits with lures

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

parts.note: to tempt is to lure

explanation.surface: An angler persists, baiting his hooks with lures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of 'baits', A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tries, puts in an effort.

clue.text: Tightens up when seeing perfect future in front of them!

definitions.meaning: perfect and future are grammatical time forms of verbs

explanation.surface: Someone braces when they see a perfect future ahead of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition gives examples of the verb forms; 'in front of them' refers to the words standing before them in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightens as muscles stiffen; perfect and future are grammatical verb forms.
